name: Famine
value: Risk of Famine in Sudan; none newly confirmed
summary: IPC alert warns of growing famine risk in Darfur and Kordofan; no area newly classified as Famine found as of 17 Nov
state: The IPC alert issued on 12–13 Oct found child acute malnutrition above the famine threshold in two South Darfur camps and emergency-level child mortality in surveyed camps, with more than 5 million people facing emergency hunger as war and El Niño-linked drought compound (IRC, 13 Oct; WHO via AllAfrica). The alert warns of a growing risk of famine but is not a new Famine classification. Searches on 17 Nov found no newer IPC Famine classification, so risk alerts keep Watch.
for_you: Most exposed are displaced families and young children in Darfur and Kordofan, where drought, blocked access and aid shortfalls combine. Famine classifications tend to follow such alerts if access does not improve.
rubric_hit: IPC 'growing risk of famine' alert for Darfur and Kordofan (Watch); no new IPC Phase 5 classification found

sources.title: War and El Niño-driven drought deplete food stocks, pushing Sudan further towards famine
Africa: IPC Sudan Food Insecurity and Malnutrition Alert

why: Famine is the most extreme humanitarian failure, almost always man-made by conflict.
drivers: War, sieges, aid access, harvest failure, funding cuts.

rubric.alert: Famine (IPC Phase 5) confirmed in at least one area.

rubric.normal: No IPC Phase 5 (Famine) classifications or projections.
